binders: Universally quantify a natural number m with 0 < m. Write V = {0,…,m−1} → ℝ for the real coordinate-vector space.
Universally quantify arbitrary types Cell and Face, potentially in different universes.
Universally quantify q : ℝ → ℝ → V and flux : V → V. The first and second real arguments of q serve as the spatial and temporal variables in the displayed integrals.
Universally quantify numericalOld : Cell → V and rule : (Cell → V) → Face → V. The rule receives the entire old numerical assignment and a face label.
Universally quantify cell ∈ Cell and leftFace, rightFace ∈ Face.
Universally quantify real endpoints a, b, s, t, subject to a < b and s < t.

Within the final conjunct, universally quantify real numbers oldBound, leftBound, rightBound, followed by three conditional norm-bound assumptions. These bounds may be chosen after all the preceding data.
There are no existential quantifiers or existential witnesses. Every average and the updated vector are explicitly defined expressions in the universally quantified data.
hypotheses: x ↦ q(x,s) and x ↦ q(x,t) are interval integrable from a to b with respect to μ = Real.measureSpace.volume.
τ ↦ flux(q(a,τ)) and τ ↦ flux(q(b,τ)) are interval integrable from s to t with respect to μ.
The vector balance ∫_a^b q(x,t) dμ(x) − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x) = ∫_s^t [flux(q(a,τ)) − flux(q(b,τ))] dμ(τ) holds.
conclusions: a < b, x ↦ q(x,s) is interval integrable from a to b, and A_s equals (b−a)⁻¹ • ∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x).
a < b, x ↦ q(x,t) is interval integrable from a to b, and A_t equals (b−a)⁻¹ • ∫_a^b q(x,t) dμ(x).
s < t, τ ↦ flux(q(a,τ)) is interval integrable from s to t, and F_L equals (t−s)⁻¹ • ∫_s^t flux(q(a,τ)) dμ(τ).

mathematical_definitions: μ denotes exactly the distinguished measure selected by Real.measureSpace. Its construction is not expanded in the packet.
For a vector-valued function h, ∫_u^v h dμ means the integral with respect to μ restricted to (u,v], minus the integral with respect to μ restricted to (v,u].
Interval integrability from u to v means integrability on both (u,v] and (v,u].
Define A_s = Avg(x ↦ q(x,s);a,b) and A_t = Avg(x ↦ q(x,t);a,b).
Define F_L = Avg(τ ↦ flux(q(a,τ));s,t) and F_R = Avg(τ ↦ flux(q(b,τ));s,t).
Define U = numericalOld(cell), G_L = rule(numericalOld,leftFace), and G_R = rule(numericalOld,rightFace).
Define Update(Δt,Δx,U,N) = U − (Δt/Δx) • N and U_new = Update(t−s,b−a,U,G_R−G_L).
All vector additions, subtractions, scalar multiplications, and equalities are coordinatewise. The notation ‖·‖_Π denotes exactly the norm extracted from the supplied Pi.normedRing instance on V.
The regional average is the restricted-measure integral multiplied by the reciprocal of the real conversion of the region's extended-nonnegative measure.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive finite number of real state coordinates, arbitrary cell and face label types, state field q, flux map, old numerical assignment, face rule, selected cell and two selected faces, and strictly increasing spatial and temporal endpoints, assume the four specified slices are interval integrable and that the change of the spatial integral equals the temporal integral of left physical flux minus right physical flux. Then all ten listed conclusions hold simultaneously: positive dimension is retained; the four explicitly defined normalized integrals satisfy their average predicates; the old spatial average and left temporal flux average agree with the corresponding measure-normalized regional integrals; the update is the old numerical vector minus the time-to-length ratio times right numerical flux minus left numerical flux; its length-weighted error relative to the new spatial average equals the old length-weighted error plus the time-weighted difference of the left and right flux errors; and any three real upper bounds on those old and boundary errors give the stated upper bound on the new error.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension is finite and strictly positive. The zero-dimensional case is excluded by hypothesis.
The intervals have strictly positive real lengths, so neither the update ratio nor the interval-average reciprocals encounter a zero denominator.

Cell and Face carry no geometry, order, adjacency, finiteness, or mesh structure. Supplying cell and the two face labels requires inhabited types for an actual instance; quantification over their elements is vacuous for empty types.
leftFace and rightFace need not be distinct, and no encoded relation identifies them geometrically with a and b or as faces of cell.

The balance equation is assumed for this single pair of spatial and temporal intervals. No differential equation, weak-solution condition on all regions, differentiability, or interior space-time integrability is asserted.
q and flux have no global continuity, measurability, or regularity requirements beyond the four composite slices' integrability.

The numerical rule is arbitrary and may depend on the entire old assignment. No locality, consistency with flux, monotonicity, accuracy order, stability condition, or restriction on the time-to-length ratio is imposed.
No assumption equates the old numerical vector with the old spatial average. Their discrepancy appears explicitly in the conclusions.
The updated vector is an expression for the selected cell, not a separately quantified new assignment or an asserted evolution across multiple steps.

The three error bounds are arbitrary real numbers. If any is negative, its corresponding norm-bound antecedent cannot hold. For actual vectors, bounds can be chosen as their norms, so the conditional estimate is not inherently vacuous.
The four average predicates repeat integrability and ordering hypotheses and equate each defined average with itself. They do not assert the existence of a point attaining the average.

Only the old spatial average and left temporal flux average are explicitly equated to regional averages; there are no corresponding regional-average conjuncts for the new spatial average or right temporal flux average.
The general regional-average definition has no explicit positive-finite-measure guard. Its behavior outside positive finite regions depends on the totalized real conversion and inverse operations.
The final estimate uses the selected product norm; the target does not quantify over arbitrary norms.
ambiguities: The supplied body of Real.measureSpace is only inferInstance. A fully independent identification of μ with Lebesgue measure, including interval-mass normalization, requires an expansion absent from the packet. The translation therefore retains μ explicitly.

Pi.normedRing inherits its norm from the unexpanded Pi.seminormedRing, and the related product additive structures also inherit unexpanded norms. The packet does not itself expose a coordinate formula that would justify replacing ‖·‖_Π by a maximum norm or another explicit formula.

MeasureTheory.integral is supplied only as MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1. Its exact integration construction and exceptional-input conventions are not recoverable from this body; the translation retains the specified integral operator.

ENNReal.toReal delegates to an unexpanded toNNReal. Its behavior at infinity is not independently specified by the displayed definition, although the target does not explicitly introduce an infinite-measure region.
